prompt:
Find what the PostgreSQL Global Development Group officially states about how long each major PostgreSQL version receives fixes. Cite the official versioning policy page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
SOURCE: https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/ | QUOTE: "The PostgreSQL Global Development Group supports a major version for 5 years after its initial release." | CLAIM: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group officially states that each major PostgreSQL version receives fixes and support for five years from its initial release date.

SOURCE: https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/ | QUOTE: "After this, a final minor version will be released and the software will then be unsupported (end-of-life)." | CLAIM: Once the five-year support period expires, the major version stops receiving fixes and is considered end-of-life.

SOURCE: https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/ | QUOTE: "Each major version receives bug fixes and, if need be, security fixes that are released at least once every three months in what we call a 'minor release.'" | CLAIM: During the five-year support window, major versions receive bug fixes and security fixes through quarterly minor releases.
